$comment: The learning systems (docs/content-data.md, COURSE-PACKS.md "Learning systems"): real-app tasks the scripts hand off with {"appTask": id}, the chapters' learning objectives (quoted from each chapter's Learning Objectives) and what covers them, the reflection before each Seal (the Key Takeaways). The quests' own done lines say what you learned, so `learned` is empty: the Logbook adds whether the app work is confirmed.

labels.kicker: Do this in the Copilot app

appTasks.title: Install the app and sign in
steps: Download and install the GitHub Copilot app for your computer.
Open it and select **Sign in to GitHub**, then sign in with your GitHub account.
At **Connect your repositories**, leave every repository unselected and select **Continue**.
appTasks.why: Every chapter starts in the app: it’s where you give Copilot’s agents their orders.

seen.prompt: Which view does the app open once you’re in?
seen.explain: The app opens the **New** view. If it shows a short tip about a new feature, you can close it.

appTasks.title: Fork the course repository
steps: Open the course repository’s fork page on GitHub.com and create your fork.
Your fork is your own copy of the repository, under your GitHub account.
appTasks.why: Your practice work lands in your own copy, not the course’s.

appTasks.title: Add your fork under Sessions
steps: In the app, select **+** next to **Sessions**, then **Add GitHub repository**.
Type `copilot-app-for-beginners` and select your fork: the result that starts with your GitHub username.
appTasks.why: The app downloads a local copy (clones it), so its sessions can work in your repository.

seen.prompt: Where does your fork show up once it’s added?
seen.explain: The app clones your fork and adds the project to the sidebar, under **Sessions**.

appTasks.title: Start your setup session
steps: Point to `copilot-app-for-beginners` in the sidebar and select the **+** that appears next to it.
In the workspace selector below the prompt box, choose **Current checkout**.
Send the short prompt from your Logbook page: name the top-level folders, and don’t change any files.
appTasks.why: This one-time setup session uses the clone that’s already on your machine.

appTasks.title: Check your tools in Terminal
steps: Select **View** > **Toggle Panel**, then **Terminal** (no tab? **+**, then **Terminal**).
Run `git --version`, `node -v`, `npm -v` and `gh --version`. Each should print a version number.
Run `gh auth status` and check it shows the account that owns your fork.
appTasks.why: The setup script and later exercises use these tools, and GitHub CLI has its own sign-in.

seen.prompt: For `node -v`, what do you compare the first number with?

options.text: The **LTS** version on the Node.js download page

seen.explain: Compare the first number with the **LTS** version on the Node.js download page. If yours is lower, install the LTS version.

appTasks.title: Enable workflows on your fork
steps: In your browser, open your fork on GitHub.com and select the **Actions** tab.
If you see **Workflows aren't being run on this forked repository**, select **I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them**.
appTasks.why: New forks turn workflows off. With them on, GitHub runs the practice exercises’ automated checks.

appTasks.title: Run the setup script
steps: In the same **Terminal** tab, from the repository root, run `node .github/scripts/setup-training-scenarios.js --dry-run`.
Check that the `Repository:` line shows your fork.
Then run `node .github/scripts/setup-training-scenarios.js --yes` and wait for `Setup complete.`
appTasks.why: Later chapters use the labels, issues, practice branches and pull requests it makes in your fork.

seen.prompt: How does the dry run end?

options.text: `Dry run complete. No changes were made.`

seen.explain: The preview ends with `Dry run complete. No changes were made.` Only `--yes` creates the practice items, and ends with `Setup complete.`

appTasks.title: Ask the agent about the course
steps: Go back to the prompt box of your project session (not Terminal).
Send the overview prompt from your Logbook page: an overview of the course repository, focused on the learning path and `samples/book-app-web`.
appTasks.why: Requests for the agent go in the prompt box; commands go in Terminal.

seen.prompt: Which folder does the summary name as the web sample for later exercises?
seen.explain: The app should summarize the course structure and identify `samples/book-app-web` as the web sample used for later exercises.

appTasks.title: Ask a question in a chat
steps: Select **+** next to **Sessions**, then **Chat**.
Check that the project picker below the prompt box shows **Chat**.
Send the prompt on your Logbook page: when to use a chat, and when a project session.
appTasks.why: Chats are for questions: no branch, no worktree, and no files change.

seen.prompt: What does the app create for a chat?
seen.explain: The app doesn’t create a branch or worktree for a chat, and no files change.

appTasks.title: Tour the sample in your project session
steps: Go back to the project session you made in Chapter 00. It’s under `copilot-app-for-beginners` in the sidebar.
Send the tour prompt on your Logbook page.
appTasks.why: The tour gives you a picture of `samples/book-app-web` before the hands-on exercises.

seen.prompt: What should the tour refer to?
seen.explain: The app should describe the sample’s purpose, technologies, main files, data flow and tests, refer to paths under `samples/book-app-web`, and leave the files unchanged.

appTasks.title: Try the model controls
steps: In your project session, select **Interactive** mode below the prompt box.
Open the model control. If **Copilot Fusion** is selected, keep **Standard**. Otherwise, select an available model and keep the default effort.
Send the prompt on your Logbook page about how `filterBooks` searches.
appTasks.why: Keep the defaults for simple tasks, and you can change the model or effort mid-session.

seen.prompt: Which file should the answer refer to?
seen.explain: It should explain that search matches titles and authors without depending on letter case, and refer to `samples/book-app-web/src/App.tsx`.

appTasks.title: Switch back to New worktree
steps: Point to the `copilot-app-for-beginners` project and select **+**.
Open the workspace selector below the prompt box and choose **New worktree**. You don’t need to send a prompt: the app keeps the choice.
appTasks.why: The app remembers your last choice, and that was **Current checkout** in Chapter 00. A new worktree keeps each session’s changes out of your main checkout.

appTasks.title: Start a session from the practice branch
steps: Point to the project and select **Create from**. On **Branches**, select `practice-empty-state-copy`.
Set **Mode** to **Plan**, type `{issue}`, select **Improve the empty state copy**, and ask for a plan.
Exit plan mode (if **Review plan** stays open, select **Continue**), run the Book App and note the empty state, then ask it to implement the plan and compare.
appTasks.why: A session from a branch, with the issue attached as context, starts with everything the task needs.

appTasks.title: Check the session with slash commands
steps: In the same session, send `/chronicle standup`.
Then send `/context`, and select the **Context** bar for its breakdown.
Ask Copilot to stop the session’s development server.
appTasks.why: They show what the session did, and how much context and AI credits it’s using.

appTasks.title: Your turn: a light and dark theme
steps: Select **Create from**, and on **Branches** select `main` for a new worktree session.
In **Plan** mode, attach `@samples/book-app-web/src` and ask for a small plan for a light and dark theme toggle, then implement it.
Check the diff and the preview in both themes, run the tests and build, then send `/chronicle standup`.
appTasks.why: The chapter’s whole workflow, on your own, without touching `main`.

appTasks.title: Check a known-good baseline
steps: Point to the `copilot-app-for-beginners` project and select **+**. Check that the workspace selector shows **New worktree**.
Set the mode to **Interactive** and ask Copilot to summarize the `@samples/book-app-web` test framework and build tool.
Select **View** > **Toggle Panel**, then **Terminal** (no tab? Select **+**, then **Terminal**).
Run `cd samples/book-app-web`, `npm install`, `npm test -- --run` and `npm run build`. If a reply shows **Run** by a snippet, you can use it.
appTasks.why: Tests and a build that pass before you change anything are your known-good baseline.

seen.explain: The course shows four passing tests. If they failed, run `npm install` in this worktree first. **Terminal** is in the review panel: select **View** > **Toggle Panel**.

appTasks.title: Fix the unread-count bug
steps: Select **Create from**, then **Branches**, then `practice-unread-count-bug`.
Type `#2` and select **Keep unread stats correct when filters are active** (another number? Type `#` and pick it by title).

In **Plan** mode, ask for a fix and validation plan. Select **Exit plan mode and I will prompt myself** (if **Review plan** stays open, select **Continue**), check the mode is **Interactive**, and ask Copilot to implement it.
Inspect **Changes**, check the tests and build, run `npm run dev`, and open **Browser** with the **Local** URL. Set **Fantasy** and **Unread**, then stop the server with `Ctrl+C`.
appTasks.why: One full inner-loop cycle: plan, change, inspect, test, build and preview.

seen.prompt: With **Fantasy** and **Unread**, what does the unread count say now?
seen.explain: The course says only **The Night Circus** shows, and the count is **1**. If it still says **5**, the fix isn’t in: check **Changes**, then reload the preview.

appTasks.title: Add a regression test
steps: In the same **Interactive** session, ask for a focused test: **Fantasy** and **Unread**, an empty search, only **The Night Circus**, and an unread count of 1.
Ask that it fails with the original bug and passes with the fix.
In **Changes**, check that it tests the visible filtered results, and doesn’t weaken an existing expectation.
Run `npm test -- --run` and `npm run build`.
appTasks.why: A regression test proves the bug would fail before the fix and pass after it.

seen.prompt: What does your new test check?

options.text: The books the filters show, and the unread count

seen.explain: The course asks for a test of the visible filtered results. If Copilot changed an old expectation, ask it to revise the test.

appTasks.title: Ask for a second opinion
steps: In the session with your fix and test, type `/` to open the slash-command palette.
Send `/rubber-duck` and ask it to critique the session’s diff, tests and browser validation, and what to check before a pull request.
Compare the critique with your evidence, and address any relevant gap.
No `/rubber-duck`? Choose a different model for the session, or send the same request without the slash command.
appTasks.why: A constructive critic finds missing evidence or assumptions before a pull request.

options.text: A critique: gaps and assumptions to check

seen.explain: The rubber duck agent critiques. You compare what it says with your evidence, and decide what to fix.

appTasks.title: Find your work in Issues and Pull requests
steps: Open **Issues** and stay on **Assigned to me**.

Select the filter icon at the right end of the tab row, then **Query filter mode** (`<>`). Add `repo:YOUR-OWNER/copilot-app-for-beginners` to the existing query (your fork’s owner), keep `state:open assignee:@me`, and press `Enter`.
Open **Pull requests**, select **Authored by me**, and add the same `repo:` term to its query: each view has its own filter.
Open a practice pull request. It shows its title, repository, number and status.
appTasks.why: Each view has its own filter, so set your fork in both.

seen.prompt: Which of these is a pull request on **Authored by me**?

options.text: Keep unread stats correct when filters are active

seen.explain: **Failing stats check practice** and **Improve empty-state copy** are the seeded pull requests. The other two are issues.

appTasks.title: From an issue to a pull request
steps: Open **Make search case-insensitive** in **Issues**. Its **New session** starts from `main`, so select **Create from**, then **Branches**, then `practice-search-case-bug`, and type `#1`.

In **Plan** mode, ask for a plan that names the files and the checks. Select **Exit plan mode and I will prompt myself** (if **Review plan** stays open, select **Continue**), check the mode is **Interactive**, and ask for the fix with a focused regression test.
Inspect **Changes**, run the tests and build, and preview: `hobbit` and `HOBBIT` give the same result. Stop the server with {key:ctrl+C}.
Ask for a pull request summary that claims only checks you saw, select **Create PR**, and don’t merge it.
appTasks.why: Main already has the fix, so this pull request is practice: it stays open.

seen.prompt: What does your pull request’s summary claim?

options.text: Only the checks I saw in the terminal or CI output

seen.explain: The course’s prompt says: don’t claim a check passed unless it appears in the terminal or CI output.

appTasks.title: Answer a review comment
steps: In **Pull requests**, on **Authored by me**, open **Improve empty-state copy** and find the comment that asks for more helpful guidance.
Select **New session** at the top of the pull request, and ask for the smallest useful change, with the diff and validation plan first.
Check that the new message answers the whole comment.
Ask Copilot to commit and push, then confirm the update on the pull request.
appTasks.why: A review comment is evidence too: answer all of it.

seen.prompt: What does the new message tell the reader?

options.text: That they can change the search term, genre or reading status
Only to change the search term

seen.explain: The whole comment asks for help with all three. If you answered it in an earlier play, the same answer stands.

appTasks.title: Fix a failing check
steps: Open **Failing stats check practice** and read the failed **Book app web** check.
Select **New session**. With your own prompt, ask Copilot to analyze the failing check and propose the smallest fix, without weakening the failing test.
Inspect the diff (favorites count for read and unread books, and the test is unchanged), then run the tests, build and preview. Stop the server.
Commit and push, then check that **Book app web** runs again and passes.
appTasks.why: Don’t mark a pull request ready until the local and GitHub evidence agree.

seen.prompt: What did **Book app web** show after your push?
seen.explain: It runs again and passes (in an earlier play, it may have passed already). No check? New forks turn workflows off: turn them on in your fork’s **Actions** tab, then push again. Still failing? Compare the Node.js version, dependencies, branch, environment variables and generated files.

appTasks.title: Your turn: both loops on a UI task
steps: Pick a small UI task: Issue 4, **Polish book card spacing and responsive layout**, with **Create from** > **Branches** > `practice-card-polish`. Did Pick & Polish already? Start from `main` and improve the filter row’s labels or helper text.
Use **Plan** mode to define one small UI improvement, then **Interactive** to build it. Inspect the diff.
Run `npm test -- --run` and `npm run build`, and preview at a wide and a narrow width (drag the review panel’s left edge).
Open a pull request whose summary lists only the validation you did, and check in **Pull requests** that its checks pass.
appTasks.why: Both loops, on your own: one focused change with honest evidence.

appTasks.title: Try Pick & Polish
steps: Select **Create from** > **Branches** > `practice-card-polish`. Run `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run dev`, and open **Browser** with the **Local** URL.
Select **Pick & Polish** in the browser toolbar, then the empty background of a book card.
Ask for a small spacing and hierarchy change, and preview it.
Inspect the diff, stop the server, and run the tests and build.
appTasks.why: A visual change still needs the same diff, test, build and browser evidence.

seen.prompt: What showed in the prompt box after you picked the card?
seen.explain: An `article.book-card` attachment appears in the prompt box, and Pick & Polish turns off.

objectives.text: Install and set up the GitHub Copilot app
Connect your fork of the course repository as a project and start a project session
Check the required tools in the app's **Terminal** tab
Run the setup script that creates the course's labels, practice issues, branches, and pull requests
Explain why you should use the GitHub Copilot app compared to using Copilot in an editor or Copilot CLI in the terminal
Identify key app features and settings
Choose between a chat and a project session for a task
Explain the session modes: Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot
Select a model and reasoning effort based on task complexity
Use prompt history to reuse and search previous prompts
Retry a response with a different model or reasoning effort
Try voice dictation (optional)
Start a worktree-backed session from a branch and attach an issue as context
Explain what a git worktree is and how it keeps each session's changes out of your `main` checkout
Add relevant context to a session so Copilot can understand the task and its supporting information
Use multiple ways to attach context: type `@` for files, `#` for issues, or drag and drop files from your computer
Decide between working in your current checkout, an isolated worktree, or a cloud sandbox
Use `/chronicle standup` and `/context` to review a session
Use the review panel, tests, build output, and browser preview to validate a local change
Run code snippets directly from Copilot's responses using the Run button or copy and paste them into the terminal
Add a regression test and ask the rubber duck agent to critique your work
Use the **Issues** and **Pull requests** views to move from an issue to a pull request
Ask GitHub Copilot to address review comments and failing checks
Explain where human judgment fits in both loops

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: The app as the control center for my agent work
The practice branches, issues and pull requests the setup script made

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: Keep my editor for deep coding, and open the app for agent work
Find my way by the work surfaces: New, Pull requests, Issues, Automations, Customize and Sessions
Chats for questions, project sessions for repository work
Interactive, Plan or Autopilot, for how much the agent does on its own
The default model and effort for simple tasks, more effort for complex work

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: Sessions as focused workspaces with their own branch, diff and history
A new worktree as my safe default
`@` for files, `#` for issues, `/` for commands

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: The inner loop: understand, change, inspect, test, build and preview
The outer loop: issue, pull request, feedback, checks and merge
The review panel: the diff, the terminal and the preview in view
Tests that protect behavior and make refactoring safer
The **Issues** and **Pull requests** views to find my work
Ready only when the diff, local validation, checks and my review agree
